narrative:
The model determined that you have a 56.9% chance of failing the bar exam on your first attempt. Because this probability is above 50%, the admissions system automatically rejected your law school application.

Three factors drove this outcome, ranked by importance. First, your decision to attend law school part-time was the strongest influence, pushing the prediction strongly toward failure. Among accepted students, only 7% planned to study part-time, while 93% attended full-time. The model sees full-time focus as much more likely to lead to passing the bar.

Second, your third-year grades placed you in the third decile of your class, noticeably below the average of roughly sixth decile among accepted students. This also pulled the prediction toward failure.

Third, your undergraduate GPA of 2.70 was lower than the 3.23 average of accepted students. In this case, however, the difference worked slightly in your favor and nudged the prediction a little toward passing, though not enough to overcome the other factors.

Taken together, your part-time status, lower class ranking in year three, and modest undergraduate grades led the model to conclude you were more likely than not to fail the bar exam, resulting in the denial of your application.

You should consider reapplying after improving your academic record, ideally switching to full-time study and raising your grades. Stronger performance in law school courses would directly address the model’s main concerns and improve your chances on a future application. (248 words)
